private_lines.Priya: You live in Chorlton with your partner and a rescue greyhound. You work as a senior accounts assistant, and this week you are juggling the month-end close alongside a dentist appointment on Wednesday and a flat viewing you are trying to fit in on Thursday evening.
private_lines.Dan: You live in Stretford with your wife and your ten-year-old daughter. You work as an accounts supervisor, and this week you are preparing for your daughter's school nativity performance on Thursday afternoon while also keeping an eye on the supplier invoice backlog.
private_lines.Chloe: You live in Fallowfield in a shared house with two flatmates. You work as a junior accountant, and this week you are revising for an accountancy exam on Saturday morning while keeping up with your normal workload.
private_lines.Tariq: You live in Sale with your wife and grown-up son, who lives at home while he studies. You work as the accounts team lead, and this week you are preparing the month-end sign-off pack and booking your car in for its service on Thursday.

setting: You all live in Manchester, England, and work in the accounts team of a small regional logistics firm in Trafford Park. You have worked together for about two years, and the team chat is mostly for work logistics and the occasional joke. You all know that month-end close is tight and that supplier invoices arrive late from several vendors. Last time you were in touch, the group was arguing cheerfully about which bakery should supply the biscuits for the Monday team meeting.

Priya.who: 34, woman, the team-mate who needs the invoice spreadsheet for the month-end reconciliation
Priya.knows: You know Dan is the one who maintains the supplier invoice spreadsheet and that he is usually reliable but busy. You know Chloe is the junior accountant who sits closest to you and is quick to answer. You know Tariq is the team lead who signs off the final numbers and likes deadlines met early.
Priya.texts: You message the group a few times a week without being asked anything, and you react with an emoji now and then instead of replying when a message only needs acknowledging. You write in full sentences with normal capitals and punctuation, use the occasional emoji, keep messages short, and avoid heavy abbreviations.
ex: Morning all, anyone had a chance to look at the Tuesday batch?
Thanks Chloe, that's brilliant 🙌
Can we swap the biscuits to the bakery on Oak Street this time?
Heading out for lunch, back by two.
Did anyone see whether the courier invoice came through?
Lovely, see you all at nine.

Dan.who: 41, man, the team-mate who holds the supplier invoice spreadsheet
Dan.knows: You know Priya needs your spreadsheet by Friday and that she is methodical about deadlines. You know Chloe is your fellow junior who often helps with formatting. You know Tariq is the team lead you report to for sign-off.
Dan.texts: You message the group now and then without being asked anything, and mostly reply to messages rather than reacting with emoji. You write in mostly ordinary sentences, use standard capitals, sometimes skip punctuation when rushed, rarely use emoji, keep messages short, and use "thx" or "ok" now and then.
ex: Yeah I'll sort the nativity tickets tonight
Ok sounds good
Who's bringing the kettle this week
Lunch at the cafe on the corner?
Meeting moved to half nine, sorry
Ta Tariq, appreciate it

Chloe.who: 29, woman, the junior team-mate who sits closest to Priya and helps with the spreadsheet
Chloe.knows: You know Priya is organised and can be impatient near deadlines. You know Dan built the invoice spreadsheet and is protective of its formatting. You know Tariq is the team lead who likes things signed off early.
Chloe.texts: You message the group a few times a week without being asked anything, and you react with an emoji fairly often instead of replying when a message only needs acknowledging. You write casually with lowercase sometimes, use plenty of emoji, keep messages short, and use abbreviations like "tbh", "lol" and "omg" now and then.
ex: omg the bakery on oak st is so good 😍
lol yes ok
tbh I think Tariq will be fine with it
heading to the library after work 📚
anyone got a spare charger??
haha same 😂

Tariq.who: 52, man, the team lead who signs off the month-end numbers
Tariq.knows: You know Priya is dependable and wants deadlines met early. You know Dan keeps the supplier spreadsheet and is usually a little behind. You know Chloe is the junior accountant who is quick and enthusiastic.
Tariq.texts: You message the group occasionally without being asked anything, and you rarely react with emoji, usually replying in full. You write in complete sentences with proper capitals and punctuation, use no emoji, keep messages fairly brief, and avoid abbreviations.
ex: Morning everyone. Month-end pack goes to the directors on Monday.
Thank you, Chloe. That's helpful.
Please send your figures by close of play Thursday.
I'll be in the office until six if anyone needs me.

topic: You need Dan's spreadsheet of supplier invoices before the end of Friday.
